units.en: Next was Prince of Ying Yougui, born of a Bozhou camp singer, commander of the left and right Crane-Controlled Armies.
units.literal: Next was Prince of Ying Yougui, whose mother was a camp entertainer from Bozhou; he was Commander of the Left and Right Crane-Controlled Armies.

units.zh: 六月丁丑朔，帝命敬翔出友珪為萊州刺史，即命之官。
units.en: On dingchou, the first of the sixth month, the Emperor ordered Jing Xiang to issue an order posting Yougui as prefect of Laizhou, and at once ordered him to take office.
units.literal: On dingchou, the first day of the sixth month, the Emperor ordered Jing Xiang to issue an order posting Yougui as prefect of Laizhou, and at once ordered him to take office.

units.zh: 己卯，矯詔稱：「博王友文謀逆，遣兵突入殿中，賴郢王友珮忠孝，將兵誅之，保全朕躬。
units.en: On jimao a forged edict read: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted revolt and burst into the hall with troops; Prince of Ying Yougui, loyal and filial, led forces to execute them and saved Us.
units.literal: On jimao a forged edict stated: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted rebellion and sent troops bursting into the hall; thanks to Prince of Ying Yougui’s loyalty and filial piety, who led troops to execute them and preserved Our person.

units.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

units.zh: 帝驚起，問：「反者為誰？」
units.en: The Emperor roused himself and cried: "Who rebels?"
units.literal: The Emperor started up and asked: "Who are the rebels?"

units.zh: 友珪僕夫馮廷諤刺帝腹，刃出於背。
units.en: Yougui's groom Feng Tingyu drove a blade into the Emperor's belly until it showed at his back.
units.literal: Yougui’s servant Feng Tingyu stabbed the Emperor in the belly; the blade came out his back.

units.zh: 友珪自以敗氈裹之，瘞於寢殿，秘不發喪。
units.en: Yougui himself wrapped the body in a cast-off rug, buried it in the hall, and concealed the death.
units.literal: Yougui himself wrapped the corpse in a worn rug, buried it in the sleeping hall, and kept the death secret.

units.zh: 友珪曰：「非他人也。」
units.en: Yougui said: "No other."
units.literal: Yougui said: "It is no other."

units.zh: 友珪曰：「老賊萬段！」
units.en: Yougui cried: "Old thief, ten thousand cuts!"
units.literal: Yougui said: "Old villain, ten thousand cuts!"

units.zh: 然疾因震驚，彌致危殆，宜令友珪權主軍國之務。」
units.en: Shock has worsened Our illness—let Yougui govern state and army affairs for now."
units.literal: Yet the illness from shock grows critical—let Yougui provisionally direct state and military affairs."

units.zh: 時左遷者多追賜死，友珪益恐。
units.en: Many recently demoted men were hunted down and forced to die; Yougui's fear deepened.
units.literal: At that time many demoted officials were pursued and granted death; Yougui grew more fearful.

units.zh: 戊寅，友珪易服微行入 左龍虎軍，見統軍韓勍，以情告之。
units.en: On wuyin Yougui went in disguise to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, confided in commander Han Qin, and laid bare his fear.
units.literal: On wuyin Yougui changed clothes and went in secret to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, saw Commander-in-Chief Han Qin, and told him his plight.

units.zh: 勍以牙兵五百人從友珪雜控鶴士入，伏於禁中；
units.en: Qin brought five hundred guardsmen; Yougui mixed them with the Crane-Controlled troops and hid them inside the palace;
units.literal: Qin led five hundred guardsmen to follow Yougui mixed among the Crane-Controlled troops into the palace; they lay in ambush within the forbidden precinct;

units.zh: 友珪葬太祖于伊闕縣，號宣陵。
units.en: Yougui buried Taizu at Yique, naming the tomb Xuan.
units.literal: Yougui buried Taizu in Yique County, titled the tomb Xuan Mausoleum.

units.zh: 李德裕因奏：「陳行泰、張絳皆令大將上奏，邀求節旄，所以必不可與。
units.en: Li Deyu then memorialized, "Both Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang had their generals petition the throne demanding commissions — for that reason they must on no account be granted.
units.literal: Li Deyu thereupon memorialized: "Chen Xingtai and Zhang Jiang both had great generals submit memorials to demand seals and credentials — therefore they must on no account be granted.

units.zh: 仲武由是威加北狄，表請於薊北立《紀聖功銘》，敕李德裕為之文，其銘曰：太和之初，赤氣宵興；
units.en: Zhongwu's prestige over the northern peoples was now supreme. He memorialized asking that a Record of Sacred Merit stele be erected north of Ji, and the court ordered Li Deyu to compose the inscription, which reads: In early Taihe crimson vapors rose at night;
units.literal: Zhongwu thereby gained authority over the northern barbarians; he memorialized requesting that a "Record of Sacred Merit" stele be erected north of Ji, and an edict ordered Li Deyu to compose the text. The inscription reads: At the beginning of Taihe, crimson vapors rose through the night;

units.zh: 今仲武上表布誠，先陳密款，因而拔用，即似有名。」
units.en: Zhongwu has now memorialized the throne with a pledge of loyalty, offering his allegiance in advance. To appoint him on that basis would seem legitimate."
units.literal: Now Zhongwu has submitted a memorial declaring his loyalty, first setting forth a secret pledge of allegiance; to promote him on that basis would seem justified."

units.zh: 開成之末，彤雲暮凝。
units.en: By the close of Kaicheng rosy clouds hung thick at dusk.
units.literal: At the end of Kaicheng, rosy clouds congealed at dusk.

units.zh: 異鳥南來，胡滅之征。
units.en: Strange birds flew from the south, portending the barbarians' destruction.
units.literal: Strange birds came from the south — a sign that the barbarians would be destroyed.

units.zh: 北夷飈掃，厥國土崩。
units.en: Northern tribes were swept away in a whirlwind, and their realm collapsed.
units.literal: Northern tribes were swept away like a storm; their state collapsed.

units.zh: 逼迫遷徙，震我邊鄙；
units.en: Driven into migration, they shook our frontier lands;
units.literal: Driven and forced to migrate, they shook our frontier districts;

units.zh: 會昌初，陳行泰殺節度使史元忠，權主留後。
units.en: Early in the Huichang era Chen Xingtai killed the military governor Shi Yuanzhong and seized control as acting administrator.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Huichang reign, Chen Xingtai killed the military governor Shi Yuanzhong and held the acting administrator's post on his own authority.

units.zh: 太祖怒，遣劉捍督戰。
units.en: The Founder, enraged, sent Liu Han to take command of the siege.
units.literal: The Founder was angry and dispatched Liu Han to supervise the battle.

units.zh: 及昭宗歸長安，朝廷議迎駕功，友寧授嶺南西道節度使，加特進、檢校司徒，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣。
units.en: After Emperor Zhaozong's return to Chang'an the court rewarded those who had escorted him: You Ning became military commissioner of Lingnan West, Special Grandee, and acting Minister of Works, with the honorific Welcoming-the-Carriage Resolute Warrior.
units.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, the court discussed merit in welcoming the imperial carriage; You Ning was given military commissioner of Lingnan West Circuit, advanced to Special Grandee and acting Minister of Works, granted the title Meritous Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.

units.zh: 三月十七日，京城軍亂，侍衛袁象先率兵入宮，友珪自殺。
units.en: On the seventeenth day of the third month the capital garrison mutinied; Palace Guard Yuan Xiangxian stormed the palace and Zhu Yougui took his own life.
units.literal: Third month, seventeenth day, capital army mutiny; Palace Guard Yuan Xiangxian led troops into the palace; Zhu Yougui killed himself.

units.zh: 張文蔚，字右華，河間人也。
units.en: Zhang Wenyu, styled Youhua, came from Hejian.
units.literal: Zhang Wenyu, style Youhua, was a native of Hejian.

units.zh: 文蔚幼礪文行，求知取友，藹然有佳士之稱。
units.en: From youth he cultivated letters and character, sought learning and worthy companions, and was known as a man of fine quality.
units.literal: As a youth Wenyu honed literary conduct, sought knowledge and chose friends, and was amiably styled an outstanding gentleman.

units.zh: 屬昭宗初還京闕，皇綱浸微，文蔚所發詔令，靡失厥中，論者多之。
units.en: When Zhaozong first came back to the capital, the throne was failing; Wenyu's edicts struck the right note every time, and men of judgment approved.
units.literal: As Zhaozong first returned to the capital, imperial governance grew weak; the edicts Wenyu drafted never missed the mark, and critics praised him.

units.zh: 文蔚殫其力解之，乃止，士人賴焉。
units.en: Wenyu spent himself to halt the slaughter, and the scholarly class owed him their lives.
units.literal: Wenyu exhausted his strength to save them and stopped it; scholars relied on him.

units.zh: 璨敗死，文蔚兼度支鹽鐵使。
units.en: After Can's fall and death, Wenyu was also made Commissioner of Finance and Salt.
units.literal: When Can fell and died, Wenyu was made concurrent Commissioner of Finance and Salt.

units.zh: 天祐四年，天子以土運將革，天命有歸，四月，命文蔚與楊涉等總率百僚，奉禪位詔至大梁。
units.en: In Tianyou 4, believing the age of earth was ending and Heaven's mandate had turned, the emperor in the fourth month sent Wenyu and Yang She at the head of the bureaucracy to Daliang with the abdication edict.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou the Son of Heaven, seeing the earthly cycle about to change and Heaven's mandate shifting, in the fourth month ordered Wenyu and Yang She to lead all officials bearing the abdication edict to Daliang.

units.zh: 太祖受命，文蔚等不易其位。
units.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Wenyu and his colleagues kept their offices.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the mandate, Wenyu and the rest kept their posts.

units.zh: 文蔚沈邃重厚，有大臣之風，居家孝且悌，雖位至清顯，與仲季相雜，在太夫人膝下，一不異布素。
units.en: Deep, grave, and weighty, he bore a great minister's air; at home he was filial and fraternal. Though he had risen to the highest offices, he sat among his brothers at their mother's knee like any man in plain cloth.
units.literal: Wenyu was deep, withdrawn, and weighty, with a great minister's bearing; at home he was filial and brotherly—though his rank reached the highest clarity, he mingled with his brothers at their mother's knee no differently from common cloth.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：張裼尚書有五子：文蔚、彝憲、濟美、仁龜，皆有名第，至宰輔丞郎。
units.en: (The 《Northern Dreams Miscellany》 says Minister Zhang Ti had five sons—Wenyu, Yixian, Jimo, and Renqi—all earned degrees and rose to chancellor or bureau chief.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Scattered Words from Northern Dreams》 says: Minister Zhang Ti had five sons—Wenyu, Yixian, Jimo, and Renqi—all held famous degrees and reached chancellors and bureau directors.)〉

units.zh: 文蔚撫視殆三十年，士君子稱之。
units.en: Wenyu tended him for nearly thirty years, to the praise of all who knew them.
units.literal: Wenyu cared for him nearly thirty years; gentlemen praised this.

units.zh: 唐乾符初，登進士第，時丞相裴坦兼判鹽鐵，解褐署巡官。
units.en: In the early Qianfu era he took the jinshi degree; Chief Minister Pei Tan, who also oversaw the salt monopoly, gave him his first appointment as a patrol official.
units.literal: Early in Tang Qianfu he passed the jinshi; when Chief Minister Pei Tan concurrently administered the salt monopoly, he received his first appointment as a patrol official under him.

units.zh: 駕還長安，除監察御史，遷左補闕侍御史、起居舍人、司勳吏部員外郎，拜司勳郎中、知制誥，歲滿授中書舍人。
units.en: After the court returned to Chang'an he rose from supervising censor through remonstrator, attendant censor, and diarist to bureau director, then Merit Director and edict drafter; a year later he became Secretariat Drafter.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Chang'an, he was made supervising censor, then promoted through Left Remonstrator, attendant censor, diarist, and bureau registrars, appointed Director of Merit and drafter of edicts, and after a full year made Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 天祐元年夏，拜中書侍郎、平章事，兼判戶部。
units.en: In summer of Tianyou 1 he was made Secretariat Vice Minister, Chief Councillor, and put in charge of Revenue.
units.literal: In the summer of the first year of Tianyou he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Chief Councillor, and concurrently administered Revenue.

units.zh: 開平二年春，暴卒於位，詔贈右僕射。
units.en: In spring of Kaiping 2 he died suddenly at his post; the court posthumously made him Right Vice Director.
units.literal: In the spring of the second year of Kaiping he died suddenly in office; an edict posthumously made him Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 未幾，以畿尉直館。
units.en: Soon he served as a capital aide and was posted to the Hanlin archive.
units.literal: Before long he was made a capital-district aide and entered the Hanlin archive.

units.zh: 丁家艱，以孝聞。
units.en: When his father died, his mourning won wide praise.
units.literal: Upon his father's death he was famed for filial piety.

units.zh: 中和歲，僖宗在蜀，大寇未滅，急於軍費，移鹽鐵於揚州，命李都就判之，奏為轉運巡官。
units.en: During the Zhonghe reign, with the emperor in Shu and rebels still unchecked, the court moved salt administration to Yangzhou under Li Du; Wenyu was named transport patrol official.
units.literal: In the Zhonghe years, with Xizong in Shu, great bandits not yet destroyed, and military funds urgent, the salt monopoly was moved to Yangzhou; Li Du was ordered to administer it, and Wenyu was recommended as transport patrol official.

units.zh: 服闋，復拜中書舍人，俄召入翰林，為承旨學士。
units.en: After mourning he resumed as Secretariat Drafter and was soon called into the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was again made Secretariat Drafter, soon summoned to the Hanlin as Academician Recipient of Edicts.

units.zh: 丁母憂，退居東畿，哀毀過禮。
units.en: He mourned his mother in the eastern suburbs, his grief so deep it outstripped the rites.
units.literal: Upon his mother's death he retired to the eastern capital suburbs, his grief exceeding ritual.

units.zh: 轉戶部侍郎，仍依前充職，尋出為禮部侍郎。
units.en: He became Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining his old duties, then moved to Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue while keeping his former duties, then sent out as Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 父裼，唐僖宗朝，累為顯官。
units.en: His father Ti rose through several high posts under Emperor Xizong of Tang.
units.literal: His father Ti, in Emperor Xizong's Tang, repeatedly held prominent offices.

units.zh: 弟濟美，早得心恙，
units.en: His brother Jimo had long suffered a disorder of the heart,
units.literal: His brother Jimo early suffered a heart ailment,

units.zh: 內一子，忘其名，少年聞壁魚食神仙字，身有五色，吞之可得仙，因欲試之，遂致心疾。
units.en: A fifth son, whose name is lost, heard as a boy that silverfish that eat sacred script turn five-colored and grant immortality if eaten; he tried it and lost his mind.
units.literal: One son, whose name is forgotten, in youth heard that booklice eating immortal characters turn five-colored and that swallowing them brings immortality; wishing to test it, he brought on a disorder of the heart.

units.zh: 子鑄，周顯德中，位至秘書監。
units.en: His son Zhuo rose to Director of the Palace Library under Later Zhou in the Xiande era.
units.literal: His son Zhuo, in Later Zhou Xiande, reached Director of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 以門下侍郎、平章事薛貽矩判建昌宮事，兼延資庫使。
units.en: Xue Yiju, vice director of the Chancellery and grand councilor, was put in charge of Jianchang Palace and named commissioner of the Yanzi Treasury as well.
units.literal: Vice director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor Xue Yiju was assigned to administer Jianchang Palace affairs and concurrently made commissioner of the Yanzi Treasury.

units.zh: 辛丑，以久雨，命宰臣薛貽矩抃定鼎門，趙光逢祠嵩嶽。
units.en: On xinchou, with rain unending, he sent Xue Yiju to worship at Dingding Gate and Zhao Guangfeng to Mount Song.
units.literal: On xinchou, because of long rain, he ordered chief ministers Xue Yiju to worship at Dingding Gate and Zhao Guangfeng at Mount Song.

units.zh: 淮陽王舅張博、魏郡太守京房坐窺道諸侯王以邪意，漏泄省中語，博要斬，房棄市。
units.en: Zhang Bo, maternal uncle of the King of Huaiyang, and Jing Fang, governor of Wei commandery, were convicted of spying on the feudal kings with evil intent and leaking palace secrets. Bo was condemned to beheading, and Fang was executed in the marketplace.
units.literal: Huaiyang King maternal uncle Zhang Bo, Wei commandery governor Jing Fang convicted spied on feudal lords kings with evil intent, leaked revealed palace secret words, Bo condemned beheaded, Fang executed in marketplace.

units.zh: 武安軍節度使馬殷進呈虔州刺史盧延昌箋表。
units.en: Ma Yin, Wuan commissioner, presented the memorial and petition of Lu Yanchang, Qianzhou prefect.
units.literal: Wuan military commissioner Ma Yin presented the memorial and petition of Qianzhou prefect Lu Yanchang.

units.zh: 諸道節度使錢鏐、張宗奭、馬殷、王審知、劉隱各賜一子六品正員官，高季昌賜一子八品正員官，賀德倫賜一子九品正員官。
units.en: Commissioners Qian Liu, Zhang Zongshi, Ma Yin, Wang Shenzhi, and Liu Yin each received a regular sixth-rank post for a son; Gao Jichang an eighth-rank post; He Delun a ninth-rank post.
units.literal: Circuit commissioners Qian Liu, Zhang Zongshi, Ma Yin, Wang Shenzhi, and Liu Yin each had one son given a regular sixth-rank post; Gao Jichang one son eighth rank; He Delun one son ninth rank.

units.zh: 大學士王鐸深知之，鐸罷相失職，樞亦久之不調。
units.en: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost his chancellorship and his position, Shu also went long without reassignment.
units.literal: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost his chancellorship and his position, Shu also went long without reassignment.

units.zh: 中和初，王鐸復見用，以舊恩徙為鄭滑掌書記、檢校司封郎中，賜金紫，入朝歷兵、吏二員外郎。
units.en: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old kindness Shu was transferred to chief secretary of Zheng-Hua and acting director of the Department of Feudal Ranks, granted gold seal and purple robe; entering court he served successively as vice director in the ministries of War and Personnel.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old kindness Shu was transferred to chief secretary of Zheng-Hua and acting Director of the Department of Feudal Ranks, granted gold seal and purple robe; entering court he served successively as vice director in the Ministries of War and Personnel.

units.zh: 廣王全昱，太祖長兄，受禪後封。
units.en: Quan Yu, Prince of Guang, was the Founder's eldest brother and received his princely title when the dynasty was founded.
units.literal: Prince of Guang Quan Yu was the Founder's eldest brother; enfeoffed after receiving the abdication.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：全昱，贈尚書令，諡德靖。
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Director of the Imperial Secretariat with the posthumous title Dejing.
units.literal: (《Five Dynasties Essentials》: Quan Yu was posthumously given Minister of Works; posthumous title Dejing.

units.zh: 《五代史闕文》：全昱，梁祖之兄也。
units.en: The 《Lacunae of the History of the Five Dynasties》 identifies Quan Yu as the Liang founder's elder brother.
units.literal: 《Lacunae of the History of the Five Dynasties》: Quan Yu was elder brother of the Liang Founder.

units.zh: 因為博戲，全昱酒酣，忽起取骰子擊盆迸散，大呼梁祖曰：「朱三，汝碭山一民，因天下饑荒，入黃巢作賊，天子用汝為四鎮節度使，富貴足矣，何故滅他李家三百年社稷，稱王稱朕，吾不忍見血吾族矣，安用博為！」
units.en: At dice play Quan Yu, drunk, leaped up, smashed the bowl with his dice, and shouted at the Liang founder: "Zhu Third! You were a peasant from Dangshan who joined Huang Chao's rebels in famine; the throne made you lord of four circuits—that should have been enough. Why wipe out the Li dynasty's three-century altars and call yourself king and Son of Heaven? I will not watch our family slaughtered—why gamble at all!"
units.literal: During gambling, Quan Yu, wine deep, suddenly rose, took dice and struck the bowl scattering them, loudly calling to the Liang Founder: "Zhu Third! You, a commoner of Dangshan—because the realm suffered famine you entered Huang Chao's bandits as a thief; the Son of Heaven used you as military commissioner of four circuits—wealth and honor are enough—why destroy the Li family's three hundred years of state altars, call yourself king and emperor? I cannot bear to see our clan's blood shed—what need for gambling!"

units.zh: 及莊宗即位，盡誅朱氏，惟全昱先令終。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong came to power he killed the whole Zhu house; only Quan Yu had already died in his bed.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he executed the entire Zhu clan; only Quan Yu had earlier died a natural death.

units.zh: 友諒，全昱子，初封衡王，後嗣廣王。
units.en: You Liang, Quan Yu's son, was first Prince of Heng and later succeeded to the title Prince of Guang.
units.literal: You Liang, son of Quan Yu, first enfeoffed Prince of Heng, later inherited Prince of Guang.

units.zh: 友能，全昱子，封惠王，後為宋、滑二州留後。
units.en: You Neng, Quan Yu's son, was created Prince of Hui and later served as acting commissioner of Song and Hua.
units.literal: You Neng, son of Quan Yu, enfeoffed Prince of Hui, later made acting commissioner of Song and Hua prefectures.

units.zh: 友誨，全昱子，封邵王。
units.en: You Hui, another son of Quan Yu, held the title Prince of Shao.
units.literal: You Hui, son of Quan Yu, enfeoffed Prince of Shao.

units.zh: 臣護按《梁史》《廣王全昱傳》曰：昱樸野，常呼帝為「三」。
units.en: Your subject Hu notes in the 《History of Liang》 biography of Prince Guang that Quan Yu was coarse and habitually addressed the emperor as "Third."
units.literal: Your subject Hu annotates: 《History of Liang》《Biography of Prince of Guang Quan Yu》 says: Yu was rustic and uncouth, often calling the Emperor "Third."

units.zh: 至道初，知單州有稱廣王之後與尼訟田者，豈以一言之善，獨存其嗣耶！）〉
units.en: Early in the Zhidao reign a man at Shan prefecture claiming descent from Prince Guang sued a nun over land—did a single honest speech alone spare his line?!)〉
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, it was known at Shan prefecture there was one claiming to be descendant of Prince of Guang disputing fields with a nun—could it be that for one good saying alone his posterity was preserved?!)〉

units.zh: 尋詣廣王於輝州，以訴其冤。
units.en: He soon sought out Prince Guang at Hui prefecture to plead his case.
units.literal: Shortly he went to Prince of Guang at Hui prefecture to plead his injustice.

units.zh: 庶人篡位，授宋州節度使。
units.en: After the commoner (Zhu Yougui) usurped the throne, Quan Yu was made military commissioner of Songzhou.
units.literal: When the commoner usurped the throne, [he] was appointed military commissioner of Songzhou.

units.zh: 王出宿至於偃師，仍詔其子衡王友諒侍從以歸。
units.en: On the road he spent a night at Yanshi; an edict also directed his son You Liang, Prince of Heng, to escort him home.
units.literal: The Prince departed, lodged overnight reaching Yanshi; moreover an edict ordered his son Prince of Heng You Liang to attend and accompany him home.

units.zh: 乾化元年，還睢陽，命內臣拜餞都外。
units.en: In the first year of Qianhua he went back to Suiyang; court eunuchs were sent outside the city to bid him farewell.
units.literal: In Qianhua year 1, he returned to Suiyang; the Emperor ordered inner-court attendants to perform farewell rites outside the capital.

units.zh: 貞明二年，卒。
units.en: He died in the second year of Zhenming.
units.literal: In Zhenming year 2, he died.
